Is the development sample adequate for the parameters spent

Source: R/sample_size.R
mm_adequacy.Rd

Reports what the specification asks a prediction model to disclose about its own size: rows, events, prevalence, the number of candidate parameters including spline and interaction terms, the expected shrinkage, and the development sample a model of this shape would need.

Usage

mm_adequacy(
  n,
  events,
  parameters,
  nagelkerke,
  likelihood_ratio = NA_real_,
  shrinkage = 0.9
)

Arguments

n

Development rows the model was fitted on, which is not the same as the rows it was handed when any are incomplete. mm_model() reads this back off the fit for that reason.

events

Outcome events among those rows.

parameters

Non-intercept model parameters.

nagelkerke

Nagelkerke R-squared from the fitted model.

likelihood_ratio

Model likelihood ratio chi-squared.

shrinkage

Target shrinkage for the requirement, conventionally 0.9.

Value

An object of class mm_adequacy.

Details

The gate is the Riley requirement from pmsampsize::pmsampsize(), not the events-per-parameter rule. Events per parameter is reported because readers expect it, and labelled as description rather than as the criterion, which is what the specification asks for.

One circularity is disclosed rather than hidden. The required sample size depends on the model's explanatory performance, which before fitting is a guess and after fitting is an estimate from the very data whose adequacy is in question. The figure here uses the fitted Nagelkerke R-squared, so it answers "was this sample adequate for the model it produced", not "how large a sample should have been collected". The second question needs an R-squared from outside these data.
